subproblem.title: Upper bound on compact sets from sub-subsequence comparisons on thin neighbourhoods (Simon 7.2.4 (13))
subproblem.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ and let μ and μ_j (j ∈ ℕ) be measures on the Borel σ-algebra of ℝ^P (evaluated on arbitrary sets as outer measures, values in [0, ∞]). Assume (a) μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^P, and (s) for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^P, every ε > 0 and every strictly increasing ψ : ℕ → ℕ there are a set W with K ⊆ W ⊆ thickening(ε, K) = {x : inf_{y∈K} |x − y| < ε} and a strictly increasing φ' : ℕ → ℕ with limsup_{i→∞} μ_{ψ(φ'(i))}(W) ≤ μ(W). Then limsup_{j→∞} μ_j(K) ≤ μ(K) for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^P (lim sup in [0, ∞]).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (μs : ℕ → Measure (Euclid P)) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)), (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → μ K < ∞) → (∀ (K : Set (Euclid P)) (ε : ℝ), IsCompact K → 0 < ε → ∀ ψ : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono ψ → ∃ W : Set (Euclid P), K ⊆ W ∧ W ⊆ thickening ε K ∧ ∃ φ' : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono φ' ∧ limsup (fun i => μs (ψ (φ' i)) W) atTop ≤ μ W) → ∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → limsup (fun j => μs j K) atTop ≤ μ K
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon 7.2.4, (13) and the remark after it (chapter-07.txt lines 264–280: limsup μ_{T_j}(K) ≤ M_{dist(·,K)<ε}(T), then ε ↓ 0; "we can repeat the argument for a subsequence of any given subsequence, hence it holds for the original sequence"). This is the measure-theoretic core of step 3(b) of the parent proof.
1. Fix a compact K ⊆ ℝ^P and put ℓ := limsup_j μ_j(K) ∈ [0, ∞]. Claim: ℓ ≤ μ(thickening(ε, K)) for every ε > 0.
2. Suppose the claim fails for some ε > 0, i.e. μ(thickening(ε, K)) < ℓ. Since [0, ∞] is densely ordered, choose b with μ(thickening(ε, K)) < b < ℓ.
3. Since b < limsup_j μ_j(K), the inequality μ_j(K) > b holds for infinitely many j (otherwise μ_j(K) ≤ b for all large j, which would force ℓ ≤ b). Listing these j in increasing order gives a strictly increasing ψ : ℕ → ℕ with μ_{ψ(i)}(K) > b for every i (Mathlib extraction_of_frequently_atTop).
4. Apply (s) to K, ε and ψ: there are W with K ⊆ W ⊆ thickening(ε, K) and a strictly increasing φ' with limsup_i μ_{ψ(φ'(i))}(W) ≤ μ(W).
5. For every i, μ_{ψ(φ'(i))}(W) ≥ μ_{ψ(φ'(i))}(K) > b, by monotonicity of the measure μ_{ψ(φ'(i))} (K ⊆ W) and step 3 applied at the index φ'(i). A sequence that is ≥ b at every index has lim sup ≥ b, so b ≤ limsup_i μ_{ψ(φ'(i))}(W).
6. Hence b ≤ limsup_i μ_{ψ(φ'(i))}(W) ≤ μ(W) ≤ μ(thickening(ε, K)) < b, using step 4 and monotonicity of μ (W ⊆ thickening(ε, K)); this contradiction proves the claim.
7. K is compact, hence closed. The set cthickening(1, K) = {x : dist(x, K) ≤ 1} is closed and bounded in ℝ^P, hence compact, so by (a), μ(thickening(1, K)) ≤ μ(cthickening(1, K)) < ∞. For a closed set K with μ(thickening(R, K)) < ∞ for some R > 0, continuity of measure from above along the decreasing sets thickening(r, K), whose intersection over r > 0 is closure(K) = K, gives μ(thickening(r, K)) → μ(K) as r ↓ 0 (Mathlib tendsto_measure_thickening_of_isClosed).
8. By the claim, ℓ ≤ μ(thickening(r, K)) for every r > 0; letting r ↓ 0 and using step 7 yields ℓ = limsup_j μ_j(K) ≤ μ(K). ∎
proof_key_steps: For fixed ε > 0, if limsup_j μ_j(K) > b > μ(thickening(ε, K)), extract a strictly increasing ψ with μ_{ψ(i)}(K) > b for all i.
Hypothesis (s) gives W ⊇ K inside thickening(ε, K) and φ' with limsup_i μ_{ψ(φ'(i))}(W) ≤ μ(W) ≤ μ(thickening(ε, K)) < b, whereas μ_{ψ(φ'(i))}(W) ≥ μ_{ψ(φ'(i))}(K) > b for all i: contradiction.
Let ε ↓ 0: μ(thickening(ε, K)) → μ(K) since K is closed and μ(thickening(1, K)) ≤ μ(cthickening(1, K)) < ∞ by (a).

audit.reason: The bad-subsequence extraction and subsequent comparison produce the stated contradiction in ENNReal. Only measure monotonicity is used for W, so its lack of a measurability hypothesis is harmless. Compact closed thickenings supply finite neighbourhood measure, allowing continuity from above to yield the exact compact-set bound.

subproblem.title: Lower semicontinuity of local mass under weak convergence on exhausting domains, along every subsequence (Simon 6.2.14 as used in 7.2.4)
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ. For j ∈ ℕ let U_j ⊆ ℝ^P be any sets and S_j ∈ 𝒟_n(U_j), and let C ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P). Assume (1) for every r ∈ ℝ, closedBall(0, r) ⊆ U_j for all sufficiently large j, and (2) S_j ⇀ C in ℝ^P (ConvergesWeakly). Then for every strictly increasing φ : ℕ → ℕ and every set O ⊆ ℝ^P, M_O(C) ≤ liminf_{i→∞} M_O(S_{φ(i)}) in [0, ∞]. Notation: 𝒟_n(V) = GeometricCurrentOn V n; 𝒟ⁿ(V) = TestFormOn V n (smooth compactly supported n-forms ω on ℝ^P with tsupport ω ⊆ V); for Y ∈ 𝒟_n(V) and any O ⊆ ℝ^P, M_O(Y) := Y.massOn O = sup{ofReal(Y(ω)) : ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(V), tsupport ω ⊆ O, |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x} ∈ [0, ∞] (SimonGMT massOn, |·| the Euclidean coefficient norm of covectors); currentEval(Y, ω) := Y(ω) if ω is a test form with tsupport ω ⊆ V and 0 otherwise; S_j ⇀ C (ConvergesWeakly Ss C) means currentEval(S_j, ω) → C(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P); thickening(ε, K) = {x : inf_{y∈K} |x − y| < ε}.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (Us : ℕ → Set (Euclid P)) (Ss : (j : ℕ) → GeometricCurrentOn (Us j) n) (C : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n), (∀ R : ℝ, ∀ᶠ j in atTop, closedBall (0 : Euclid P) R ⊆ Us j) → ConvergesWeakly Ss C → ∀ φ : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono φ → ∀ O : Set (Euclid P), C.massOn O ≤ liminf (fun i => (Ss (φ i)).massOn O) atTop
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, 2.14 (chapter-06.txt lines 313–316: M_W(T) ≤ liminf_q M_W(T_q) under weak convergence), as invoked in the proof of 7.2.4 for (8) and (14) (chapter-07.txt lines 262–263 and 281–283). This is step (L3) of the parent proof, for currents on the varying domains U_j. The parent states (L3) for bounded open O, but its argument only uses that tsupport ω ⊆ U_j for large j, which already follows from the compactness of tsupport ω; hence the claim holds for every set O.
1. By definition M_O(C) is the supremum in [0, ∞] of ofReal(C(ω)) over the set A := massAdmissibleOn(ℝ^P, n, O) of ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) with tsupport ω ⊆ O and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x. So it suffices to show ofReal(C(ω)) ≤ L := liminf_i M_O(S_{φ(i)}) for every ω ∈ A (a supremum of values each ≤ L is ≤ L).
2. Fix ω ∈ A. Being a test form, ω has compact support, so tsupport ω is compact, hence bounded: tsupport ω ⊆ closedBall(0, r) for some r ∈ ℝ.
3. By (1) there is j₀ with closedBall(0, r) ⊆ U_j for all j ≥ j₀. As φ is strictly increasing, φ(i) ≥ i for every i (so φ(i) → ∞), hence closedBall(0, r) ⊆ U_{φ(i)} and therefore tsupport ω ⊆ U_{φ(i)} for all i ≥ j₀.
4. Let i ≥ j₀. Since ω is a test form with tsupport ω ⊆ U_{φ(i)}, the definition of currentEval gives currentEval(S_{φ(i)}, ω) = S_{φ(i)}(ω_i), where ω_i ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U_{φ(i)}) is the same form ω regarded as a test form in U_{φ(i)}. Since tsupport ω_i = tsupport ω ⊆ O and |ω_i(x)| = |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x, ω_i ∈ massAdmissibleOn(U_{φ(i)}, n, O), so ofReal(currentEval(S_{φ(i)}, ω)) = ofReal(S_{φ(i)}(ω_i)) ≤ M_O(S_{φ(i)}) (each admissible value is at most the supremum).
5. By (2), currentEval(S_j, ω) → C(ω) as j → ∞; since φ(i) → ∞, also currentEval(S_{φ(i)}, ω) → C(ω) as i → ∞, and by continuity of ofReal : ℝ → [0, ∞], a_i := ofReal(currentEval(S_{φ(i)}, ω)) → ofReal(C(ω)). The liminf of a convergent sequence in [0, ∞] is its limit, so ofReal(C(ω)) = liminf_i a_i.
6. By step 4, a_i ≤ M_O(S_{φ(i)}) for all i ≥ j₀; the liminf is monotone under eventual inequalities (in the complete lattice [0, ∞] no boundedness side conditions arise), so liminf_i a_i ≤ L, i.e. ofReal(C(ω)) ≤ L by step 5.
7. As ω ∈ A was arbitrary, step 1 gives M_O(C) ≤ liminf_i M_O(S_{φ(i)}). ∎
proof_key_steps: Reduce to one admissible form ω for C in O, since M_O(C) is a supremum.
tsupport ω is compact, so by (1) and φ(i) → ∞ it lies in U_{φ(i)} for all large i; there ω is admissible for S_{φ(i)} in O and ofReal(currentEval(S_{φ(i)}, ω)) ≤ M_O(S_{φ(i)}).
By (2) along φ, ofReal(currentEval(S_{φ(i)}, ω)) → ofReal(C(ω)); pass to the liminf and take the supremum over ω.

audit.reason: The stronger arbitrary-set statement is justified. Each admissible form has compact support, so exhaustion places it in the varying domains eventually along every strictly increasing subsequence. Weak convergence, continuity of ofReal, eventual monotonicity of liminf and the defining supremum prove the claim without openness or boundedness of O.

subproblem.title: Semicontinuity of the mass measures along the sequence: finiteness and lim sup bound on compacts, lim inf bound on open sets (Simon 7.2.4 (13), (14))
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ. For j ∈ ℕ let U_j ⊆ ℝ^P be open and S_j ∈ 𝒟_n(U_j), and let C ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P). Assume (1) for every r ∈ ℝ, closedBall(0, r) ⊆ U_j for all sufficiently large j; (2) S_j ⇀ C in ℝ^P (ConvergesWeakly); (3) (local comparison) for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^P, every ε > 0 and every strictly increasing ψ : ℕ → ℕ there are an open W with K ⊆ W ⊆ thickening(ε, K) and a strictly increasing φ' : ℕ → ℕ such that limsup_i M_W(S_{ψ(φ'(i))}) ≤ M_W(S) for every integer multiplicity S ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with SameBoundary S C (∂S = ∂C if n ≥ 1, vacuous if n = 0) and spt(S − C) ⊆ K. Let R_j be an integer multiplicity representation of S_j in U_j for every j (R_j : IMRep U_j n with R_j.Represents S_j) and R an integer multiplicity representation of C in ℝ^P; put μ_j := R_j.measure = θ_j Hⁿ⌞M_j and μ := R.measure = θ Hⁿ⌞M. Then (a) μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^P; (b) limsup_j μ_j(K) ≤ μ(K) for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^P; (c) μ(G) ≤ liminf_j μ_j(G) for every open G ⊆ ℝ^P (lim sup and lim inf in [0, ∞]). Notation: 𝒟_n(V) = GeometricCurrentOn V n; 𝒟ⁿ(V) = TestFormOn V n (smooth compactly supported n-forms ω on ℝ^P with tsupport ω ⊆ V); for Y ∈ 𝒟_n(V) and any O ⊆ ℝ^P, M_O(Y) := Y.massOn O = sup{ofReal(Y(ω)) : ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(V), tsupport ω ⊆ O, |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x} ∈ [0, ∞] (SimonGMT massOn, |·| the Euclidean coefficient norm of covectors); currentEval(Y, ω) := Y(ω) if ω is a test form with tsupport ω ⊆ V and 0 otherwise; S_j ⇀ C (ConvergesWeakly Ss C) means currentEval(S_j, ω) → C(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P); thickening(ε, K) = {x : inf_{y∈K} |x − y| < ε}.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (Us : ℕ → Set (Euclid P)) (Ss : (j : ℕ) → GeometricCurrentOn (Us j) n) (C : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n), (∀ j, IsOpen (Us j)) → (∀ R : ℝ, ∀ᶠ j in atTop, closedBall (0 : Euclid P) R ⊆ Us j) → ConvergesWeakly Ss C → (∀ (K : Set (Euclid P)) (ε : ℝ), IsCompact K → 0 < ε → ∀ ψ : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono ψ → ∃ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W ∧ K ⊆ W ∧ W ⊆ thickening ε K ∧ ∃ φ' : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono φ' ∧ ∀ S : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n, IsIntegerMultiplicity S → SameBoundary S C → (S - C).support ⊆ K → limsup (fun j => (Ss (ψ (φ' j))).massOn W) atTop ≤ S.massOn W) → ∀ Rs : (j : ℕ) → IMRep (Us j) n, (∀ j, (Rs j).Represents (Ss j)) → ∀ R : IMRep (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n, R.Represents C → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → R.measure K < ∞) ∧ (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → limsup (fun j => (Rs j).measure K) atTop ≤ R.measure K) ∧ (∀ G : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen G → R.measure G ≤ liminf (fun j => (Rs j).measure G) atTop)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon 7.2.4 (13), (14) (chapter-07.txt lines 264–284); steps 3(a)–(c) of the parent proof. Statement (c) is proved for every open G (the parent needs it only for bounded G) because the sibling mass_lsc holds for every set. Siblings used: mass_equals_rep_measure (accepted cmc_massOn_eq_imRep_measure: if U ⊆ ℝ^P is open and R represents T ∈ 𝒟_n(U), then M_W(T) = R.measure(W) for every open W ⊆ ℝ^P), mass_lsc and limsup_criterion.
1. (Masses on open sets are weights.) ℝ^P is open and R represents C, so M_G(C) = μ(G) for every open G ⊆ ℝ^P; for each j, U_j is open and R_j represents S_j, so M_G(S_j) = μ_j(G) for every open G ⊆ ℝ^P (mass_equals_rep_measure).
2. (a) Let K ⊆ ℝ^P be compact. K is closed, hence Borel, so by the definition of a measure with density and of restriction, μ(K) = ∫_K θ d(Hⁿ⌞M) = ∫_{K∩M} θ dHⁿ = ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ. Since K is compact and K ⊆ ℝ^P, the field locallyIntegrable_mult of R gives ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ ≠ ∞. Hence μ(K) < ∞.
3. (C is an admissible competitor for itself.) C is integer multiplicity, witnessed by R. SameBoundary C C holds: for n = 0 it is True by definition, and for n = m + 1 it is the equality ∂C = ∂C. Moreover spt(C − C) = ∅: by definition spt(C − C) = ℝ^P ∖ Z, where Z is the union of the open sets V with closure V compact and contained in ℝ^P on which C − C vanishes; for x ∈ ℝ^P the ball B(x, 1) is open, its closure lies in the compact closed ball closedBall(x, 1) and is therefore compact, and C − C vanishes on it because (C − C)(ω) = C(ω) − C(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P); so x ∈ Z. In particular spt(C − C) ⊆ K for every set K.
4. (b) Apply the sibling limsup_criterion to the measures μ_j and μ. Its hypothesis (a) is step 2. For its hypothesis (s), let K be compact, ε > 0 and ψ strictly increasing. Hypothesis (3) applied to K, ε, ψ gives an open W with K ⊆ W ⊆ thickening(ε, K) and a strictly increasing φ' such that limsup_i M_W(S_{ψ(φ'(i))}) ≤ M_W(S) for every admissible S; by step 3 we may take S := C, which gives limsup_i M_W(S_{ψ(φ'(i))}) ≤ M_W(C). Since W is open, step 1 rewrites every term: M_W(S_{ψ(φ'(i))}) = μ_{ψ(φ'(i))}(W) for every i, and M_W(C) = μ(W). Hence limsup_i μ_{ψ(φ'(i))}(W) ≤ μ(W), so W and φ' witness (s). The conclusion of limsup_criterion is exactly (b).
5. (c) Let G ⊆ ℝ^P be open. The sibling mass_lsc with φ := id and O := G (its hypotheses are (1) and (2)) gives M_G(C) ≤ liminf_j M_G(S_j). By step 1, M_G(C) = μ(G) and M_G(S_j) = μ_j(G) for every j, so μ(G) ≤ liminf_j μ_j(G). ∎
proof_key_steps: Masses on open sets equal the weights of the representations (mass_equals_rep_measure).
(a): μ(K) = ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞ by local integrability of the multiplicity of R.
(b): C is an admissible competitor for itself (integer multiplicity via R, SameBoundary C C, spt(C − C) = ∅); hypothesis (3) with S = C, rewritten into weights, is hypothesis (s) of limsup_criterion.
(c): mass_lsc with φ = id, rewritten into weights.

subproblem.title: The weak limit is minimizing in ℝ^P (Simon 7.2.4 (8))
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ. For j ∈ ℕ let U_j ⊆ ℝ^P be any sets and S_j ∈ 𝒟_n(U_j), and let C ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) be integer multiplicity. Assume (1) for every r ∈ ℝ, closedBall(0, r) ⊆ U_j for all sufficiently large j; (2) S_j ⇀ C in ℝ^P (ConvergesWeakly); (3) (local comparison) for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^P, every ε > 0 and every strictly increasing ψ : ℕ → ℕ there are an open W with K ⊆ W ⊆ thickening(ε, K) and a strictly increasing φ' : ℕ → ℕ such that limsup_i M_W(S_{ψ(φ'(i))}) ≤ M_W(S) for every integer multiplicity S ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with SameBoundary S C (∂S = ∂C if n ≥ 1, vacuous if n = 0) and spt(S − C) ⊆ K. Then C is minimizing in ℝ^P (IsMinimizingIn C univ): C is integer multiplicity, and M_W(C) ≤ M_W(S) whenever W ⊆ ℝ^P is open with closure W compact (CompactlyContained W ℝ^P), S ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) is integer multiplicity, SameBoundary S C, spt(S − C) is compact and spt(S − C) ⊆ ℝ^P ∩ W. Notation: 𝒟_n(V) = GeometricCurrentOn V n; 𝒟ⁿ(V) = TestFormOn V n (smooth compactly supported n-forms ω on ℝ^P with tsupport ω ⊆ V); for Y ∈ 𝒟_n(V) and any O ⊆ ℝ^P, M_O(Y) := Y.massOn O = sup{ofReal(Y(ω)) : ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(V), tsupport ω ⊆ O, |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x} ∈ [0, ∞] (SimonGMT massOn, |·| the Euclidean coefficient norm of covectors); currentEval(Y, ω) := Y(ω) if ω is a test form with tsupport ω ⊆ V and 0 otherwise; S_j ⇀ C (ConvergesWeakly Ss C) means currentEval(S_j, ω) → C(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P); thickening(ε, K) = {x : inf_{y∈K} |x − y| < ε}.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (Us : ℕ → Set (Euclid P)) (Ss : (j : ℕ) → GeometricCurrentOn (Us j) n) (C : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n), (∀ R : ℝ, ∀ᶠ j in atTop, closedBall (0 : Euclid P) R ⊆ Us j) → IsIntegerMultiplicity C → ConvergesWeakly Ss C → (∀ (K : Set (Euclid P)) (ε : ℝ), IsCompact K → 0 < ε → ∀ ψ : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono ψ → ∃ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W ∧ K ⊆ W ∧ W ⊆ thickening ε K ∧ ∃ φ' : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono φ' ∧ ∀ S : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n, IsIntegerMultiplicity S → SameBoundary S C → (S - C).support ⊆ K → limsup (fun j => (Ss (ψ (φ' j))).massOn W) atTop ≤ S.massOn W) → IsMinimizingIn C univ
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon 7.2.4 (8)–(12) and the lower-semicontinuity step after (12) (chapter-07.txt lines 222–263); step 1 of the parent proof. Siblings used: mass_lsc (M_O(C) ≤ liminf_i M_O(S_{φ(i)}) for every set O and strictly increasing φ, under (1), (2)) and minimality_localizes (accepted cmc_massOn_le_of_le_near_support: if U ⊆ ℝ^P is open, S, T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) are integer multiplicity, K is compact with spt(S − T) ⊆ K, W ⊆ W' are open with K ⊆ W, closure W' compact and contained in U, and M_W(T) ≤ M_W(S), then M_{W'}(T) ≤ M_{W'}(S)). The latter packages exactly the locality argument (L4) and the additivity computation M_W(C) = μ_C(W') + μ_C(W ∖ W') ≤ … of parent step 1.
1. The first component of IsMinimizingIn C ℝ^P, that C is integer multiplicity, is a hypothesis.
2. Let W ⊆ ℝ^P be open with closure W compact (and closure W ⊆ ℝ^P), let S ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) be integer multiplicity with SameBoundary S C, and suppose K := spt(S − C) is compact with K ⊆ ℝ^P ∩ W, so K ⊆ W. We must show M_W(C) ≤ M_W(S).
3. Since K is compact, W is open and K ⊆ W, there is ε > 0 with thickening(ε, K) ⊆ W (a compact subset of an open set has a uniform metric neighbourhood inside it; Mathlib IsCompact.exists_thickening_subset_open).
4. Apply hypothesis (3) to K, ε and the strictly increasing map ψ := id. It yields an open W' with K ⊆ W' ⊆ thickening(ε, K) and a strictly increasing φ' such that limsup_i M_{W'}(S_{φ'(i)}) ≤ M_{W'}(S') for every admissible competitor S'. The current S is admissible: it is integer multiplicity, SameBoundary S C holds, and spt(S − C) = K ⊆ K. Hence limsup_i M_{W'}(S_{φ'(i)}) ≤ M_{W'}(S).
5. The sibling mass_lsc, applied with φ := φ' and O := W' (its hypotheses are (1) and (2)), gives M_{W'}(C) ≤ liminf_i M_{W'}(S_{φ'(i)}). For every sequence in [0, ∞], liminf ≤ limsup along atTop. Therefore M_{W'}(C) ≤ liminf_i M_{W'}(S_{φ'(i)}) ≤ limsup_i M_{W'}(S_{φ'(i)}) ≤ M_{W'}(S).
6. Apply the sibling minimality_localizes (cmc_massOn_le_of_le_near_support, whose frozen statement names the smaller open set W and the larger one W') with the instantiation (U, S, T, K, W, W') := (ℝ^P, S, C, K, W', W), where W' is the open set from step 4 and W the given open set: ℝ^P is open; S and C are integer multiplicity; K is compact and spt(S − C) ⊆ K; W' and W are open; K ⊆ W' by step 4; W' ⊆ thickening(ε, K) ⊆ W by steps 3–4; closure W is compact and contained in ℝ^P (CompactlyContained W ℝ^P); and M_{W'}(C) ≤ M_{W'}(S) by step 5. Its conclusion is M_W(C) ≤ M_W(S).
7. Since W and S were arbitrary, C is minimizing in ℝ^P. ∎
proof_key_steps: Given an admissible pair (W, S), K := spt(S − C) ⊆ W is compact; choose ε > 0 with thickening(ε, K) ⊆ W.

Hypothesis (3) with ψ = id and the competitor S gives an open W' ⊇ K inside thickening(ε, K) and φ' with limsup_i M_{W'}(S_{φ'(i)}) ≤ M_{W'}(S); mass_lsc and liminf ≤ limsup give M_{W'}(C) ≤ M_{W'}(S).
minimality_localizes transfers M_{W'}(C) ≤ M_{W'}(S) from W' to W.

audit.reason: The proof correctly chooses a thin neighbourhood inside the prescribed comparison region, applies local comparison with the identity subsequence, and combines mass_lsc with liminf ≤ limsup. The explicit localization instantiation transfers the inequality to the original region. It uses exactly the declared dependencies and proves IsMinimizingIn, including integer multiplicity.
